sanskrit: mitraiḥ saha virodhaṃ ca prāpnute tejasāvṛtaḥ prāpnoti dveṣyatāṃ caiva lokāt svajanatas tathā
english: Enveloped in wrath, he falls into conflict even with his friends, and becomes an object of hatred both from the world and from his own kinsmen.

sanskrit: so 'vamānād arthahānim upālambham anādaram saṃtāpadveṣalobhāṃś ca śatrūṃś ca labhate naraḥ
english: From contempt, that man gains loss of wealth, reproach, disrespect, grief, hatred, greed, and enemies.

sanskrit: krodhād daṇḍān manuṣyeṣu vividhān puruṣo nayan bhraśyate śīghram aiśvaryāt prāṇebhyaḥ svajanād api
english: A man who inflicts various punishments on people out of anger quickly falls from his sovereignty, his life, and his own kindred.

sanskrit: yo 'pakartṝṃś ca kartṝṃś ca tejasaivopagacchati tasmād udvijate lokaḥ sarpād veśmagatād iva
english: He who approaches both those who harm and those who help with sheer force — people shrink from him just as from a serpent that has entered the house.

sanskrit: yasmād udvijate lokaḥ kathaṃ tasya bhavo bhavet antaraṃ hy asya dṛṣṭvaiva loko vikurute dhruvam tasmān nātyutsṛjet tejo na ca nityaṃ mṛdur bhavet
english: How can prosperity come to one from whom the world recoils? For when people see any opening, they will surely act against him. Therefore one should neither always unleash fierceness, nor should one always be gentle.

sanskrit: kāle mṛdur yo bhavati kāle bhavati dāruṇaḥ sa vai sukham avāpnoti loke 'muṣminn ihaiva ca
english: He who is gentle at the right time and harsh at the right time truly attains happiness both in this world and in the next.

sanskrit: kṣamākālāṃs tu vakṣyāmi śṛṇu me vistareṇa tān ye te nityam asaṃtyājyā yathā prāhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: Now I shall speak to you at length of the times for forbearance — those occasions that must never be abandoned, as the wise have declared.

sanskrit: pūrvopakārī yas tu syād aparādhe 'garīyasi upakāreṇa tat tasya kṣantavyam aparādhinaḥ
english: If one who has previously done a benefit commits an offense that is not too grave, his transgression should be forgiven in return for that earlier service.

sanskrit: abuddhim āśritānāṃ ca kṣantavyam aparādhinām na hi sarvatra pāṇḍityaṃ sulabhaṃ puruṣeṇa vai
english: The offenses of those who acted out of ignorance should be forgiven, for wisdom is not easily attained by every person in every situation.

sanskrit: atha ced buddhijaṃ kṛtvā brūyus te tad abuddhijam pāpān svalpe 'pi tān hanyād aparādhe tathānṛjūn
english: But if those who commit a deliberate wrong then claim it arose from ignorance — those wicked and dishonest men should be punished even for a minor offense.

sanskrit: sarvasyaiko 'parādhas te kṣantavyaḥ prāṇino bhavet dvitīye sati vadhyas tu svalpe 'py apakṛte bhavet
english: A single offense by any living being should be forgiven; but if he offends a second time, he deserves to be punished, even if the harm done is small.

sanskrit: ajānatā bhavet kaś cid aparādhaḥ kṛto yadi kṣantavyam eva tasyāhuḥ suparīkṣya parīkṣayā
english: If any offense was committed unknowingly, the wise say it should certainly be forgiven — but only after careful investigation.

sanskrit: mṛdunā mārdavaṃ hanti mṛdunā hanti dāruṇam nāsādhyaṃ mṛdunā kiṃ cit tasmāt tīkṣṇataro mṛduḥ
english: Gentleness conquers the gentle; gentleness conquers even the harsh. There is nothing that cannot be accomplished by gentleness; thus gentleness is sharper than sharpness.

sanskrit: deśakālau tu saṃprekṣya balābalam athātmanaḥ nādeśakāle kiṃ cit syād deśaḥ kālaḥ pratīkṣyate tathā lokabhayāc caiva kṣantavyam aparādhinaḥ
english: Having considered place and time and one's own strength and weakness, one should not act at the wrong place or time — place and time must be awaited. Likewise, an offender should be forgiven out of fear of the people's reaction.

sanskrit: eta evaṃvidhāḥ kālāḥ kṣamāyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ ato 'nyathānuvartatsu tejasaḥ kāla ucyate
english: These are the enumerated occasions for forbearance. In all other situations where people act contrary to these, it is said to be the time for the display of energy.

sanskrit: draupady uvāca tad ahaṃ tejasaḥ kālaṃ tava manye narādhipa dhārtarāṣṭreṣu lubdheṣu satataṃ cāpakāriṣu
english: Draupadī said: That, I believe, is exactly the time for your energy, O king — with the Dhārtarāṣṭras who are ever greedy and ever harmful.

sanskrit: na hi kaś cit kṣamākālo vidyate 'dya kurūn prati tejasaś cāgate kāle teja utsraṣṭum arhasi
english: For there is no occasion for forbearance now toward the Kurus. The time for energy has arrived — you ought to release that energy.

sanskrit: mṛdur bhavaty avajñātas tīkṣṇād udvijate janaḥ kāle prāpte dvayaṃ hy etad yo veda sa mahīpatiḥ
english: The gentle man is despised; people recoil from the fierce man. He who knows how to use both at the right time — he is a true king of the earth.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca krodho hantā manuṣyāṇāṃ krodho bhāvayitā punaḥ iti viddhi mahāprājñe krodhamūlau bhavābhavau
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Know this, O greatly wise one — anger is the destroyer of men, yet anger is also their sustainer. Both existence and non-existence are rooted in anger.

sanskrit: yo hi saṃharate krodhaṃ bhāvas tasya suśobhane yaḥ punaḥ puruṣaḥ krodhaṃ nityaṃ na sahate śubhe tasyābhāvāya bhavati krodhaḥ paramadāruṇaḥ
english: For the man who restrains anger, O lovely one, there is flourishing. But the man who can never endure anger, O auspicious one — for him anger becomes most terribly destructive.

sanskrit: krodhamūlo vināśo hi prajānām iha dṛśyate tat kathaṃ mādṛśaḥ krodham utsṛjel lokanāśanam
english: The destruction of creatures in this world is seen to be rooted in anger. How then could one like me release that anger which destroys the world?

sanskrit: kruddhaḥ pāpaṃ naraḥ kuryāt kruddho hanyād gurūn api kruddhaḥ paruṣayā vācā śreyaso 'py avamanyate
english: An angry man commits sin; an angry man may even slay his elders; an angry man with harsh words insults even his superiors.

sanskrit: vācyāvācye hi kupito na prajānāti karhi cit nākāryam asti kruddhasya nāvācyaṃ vidyate tathā
english: When enraged, a man never knows what ought to be said and what ought not to be said. For one who is angry, there is nothing that cannot be done and nothing that cannot be said.

sanskrit: hiṃsyāt krodhād avadhyāṃś ca vadhyān saṃpūjayed api ātmānam api ca kruddhaḥ preṣayed yamasādanam
english: Out of anger one may harm those who should not be harmed, and honor those who deserve to be slain. An angry man may even send himself to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: etān doṣān prapaśyadbhir jitaḥ krodho manīṣibhiḥ icchadbhiḥ paramaṃ śreya iha cāmutra cottamam
english: Seeing these faults, anger has been conquered by the wise who desire the highest good here and the best in the next world.

sanskrit: taṃ krodhaṃ varjitaṃ dhīraiḥ katham asmadvidhaś caret etad draupadi saṃdhāya na me manyuḥ pravardhate
english: How could one like me practice that anger which the steadfast have renounced? Bearing all this in mind, Draupadī, my anger does not grow.

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ ca paraṃ caiva trāyate mahato bhayāt krudhyantam apratikrudhyan dvayor eṣa cikitsakaḥ
english: He who does not return anger to one who is angry saves both himself and the other from great danger — he is the healer of both.

sanskrit: mūḍho yadi kliśyamānaḥ krudhyate 'śaktimān naraḥ balīyasāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ tyajaty ātmānam antataḥ
english: If a foolish and powerless man grows angry when afflicted, he ultimately destroys himself before those who are more powerful.

sanskrit: tasyātmānaṃ saṃtyajato lokā naśyanty anātmanaḥ tasmād draupady aśaktasya manyor niyamanaṃ smṛtam
english: For one bereft of self who abandons himself, the worlds are lost. Therefore, Draupadī, it is prescribed that one who lacks power must restrain his anger.

sanskrit: vidvāṃs tathaiva yaḥ śaktaḥ kliśyamāno na kupyati sa nāśayitvā kleṣṭāraṃ paraloke ca nandati
english: Likewise, the learned and powerful man who does not become angry when afflicted — having destroyed his tormentor, he rejoices in the next world.

sanskrit: tasmād balavatā caiva durbalena ca nityadā kṣantavyaṃ puruṣeṇāhur āpatsv api vijānatā
english: Therefore the wise say that a man — whether powerful or weak — must always be forbearing, even in adversity.

sanskrit: manyor hi vijayaṃ kṛṣṇe praśaṃsantīha sādhavaḥ kṣamāvato jayo nityaṃ sādhor iha satāṃ matam
english: The virtuous here praise the conquest of anger, O Kṛṣṇā. It is the abiding view of the good and the righteous that victory forever belongs to the forbearing.

sanskrit: satyaṃ cānṛtataḥ śreyo nṛśaṃsāc cānṛśaṃsatā tam evaṃ bahudoṣaṃ tu krodhaṃ sādhuvivarjitam mādṛśaḥ prasṛjet kasmāt suyodhanavadhād api
english: Truth is better than falsehood, and kindness better than cruelty. How then could one like me release that anger, so full of faults and abandoned by the virtuous — even for the slaying of Suyodhana?

sanskrit: tejasvīti yam āhur vai paṇḍitā dīrghadarśinaḥ na krodho 'bhyantaras tasya bhavatīti viniścitam
english: Him whom the learned, far-sighted men call truly energetic — it is certain that anger does not dwell within him.

sanskrit: yas tu krodhaṃ samutpannaṃ prajñayā pratibādhate tejasvinaṃ taṃ vidvāṃso manyante tattvadarśinaḥ
english: He who repels anger as it arises by means of wisdom — the learned who see the truth consider him to be truly energetic.

sanskrit: kruddho hi kāryaṃ suśroṇi na yathāvat prapaśyati na kāryaṃ na ca maryādāṃ naraḥ kruddho 'nupaśyati
english: An angry man, O fair-hipped one, does not see his duty as it truly is; an angry man perceives neither duty nor the boundaries of proper conduct.

sanskrit: hanty avadhyān api kruddho gurūn rūkṣais tudaty api tasmāt tejasi kartavye krodho dūrāt pratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: An angry man slays even those who should not be slain, and wounds even his elders with harsh words. Therefore, when energy is to be exercised, anger should be kept at a great distance.

sanskrit: dākṣyaṃ hy amarṣaḥ śauryaṃ ca śīghratvam iti tejasaḥ guṇāḥ krodhābhibhūtena na śakyāḥ prāptum añjasā
english: Skill, intolerance of wrong, courage, and swiftness — these are the qualities of energy. They cannot straightforwardly be attained by one overwhelmed by anger.

sanskrit: krodhaṃ tyaktvā tu puruṣaḥ samyak tejo 'bhipadyate kālayuktaṃ mahāprājñe kruddhais tejaḥ suduḥsaham
english: Having abandoned anger, a man properly attains energy suited to the occasion, O greatly wise one. Energy wielded by the angry is very hard to bear.

sanskrit: krodhas tv apaṇḍitaiḥ śaśvat teja ity abhidhīyate rajas tal lokanāśāya vihitaṃ mānuṣān prati
english: But anger is constantly called energy by the unlearned — that is the quality of rajas, ordained for the destruction of people in the world.

sanskrit: tasmāc chaśvat tyajet krodhaṃ puruṣaḥ samyag ācaran śreyān svadharmānapago na kruddha iti niścitam
english: Therefore a man who acts rightly should always abandon anger. It is certain that one who does not deviate from his own duty without anger is better.

sanskrit: yadi sarvam abuddhīnām atikrāntam amedhasām atikramo madvidhasya kathaṃ svit syād anindite
english: If all the transgressions are those of the unintelligent and the witless, how, O blameless one, could there be a transgression by one such as I?

sanskrit: yadi na syur manuṣyeṣu kṣamiṇaḥ pṛthivīsamāḥ na syāt saṃdhir manuṣyāṇāṃ krodhamūlo hi vigrahaḥ
english: If there were no forbearing men among humans, patient as the earth, there would be no reconciliation among people — for quarrels are rooted in anger.

sanskrit: abhiṣakto hy abhiṣajed āhanyād guruṇā hataḥ evaṃ vināśo bhūtānām adharmaḥ prathito bhavet
english: One who is abused would abuse in return; one who is struck by a senior would strike back. Thus the destruction of beings would spread, and unrighteousness would be proclaimed.

sanskrit: ākruṣṭaḥ puruṣaḥ sarvaḥ pratyākrośed anantaram pratihanyād dhataś caiva tathā hiṃsyāc ca hiṃsitaḥ
english: Every man who is reviled would revile in turn; one who is struck would strike back; one who is harmed would cause harm in return.

sanskrit: hanyur hi pitaraḥ putrān putrāś cāpi tathā pitṝn hanyuś ca patayo bhāryāḥ patīn bhāryās tathaiva ca
english: Fathers would slay sons and sons would slay fathers in return; wives would slay husbands and husbands would slay wives.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃkupite loke janma kṛṣṇe na vidyate prajānāṃ saṃdhimūlaṃ hi janma viddhi śubhānane
english: In a world thus inflamed with anger, O Kṛṣṇā, there would be no birth. For know, O fair-faced one, that birth is the very root of the continuity of creatures.

sanskrit: tāḥ kṣīyeran prajāḥ sarvāḥ kṣipraṃ draupadi tādṛśe tasmān manyur vināśāya prajānām abhavāya ca
english: In such a state, all creatures would quickly perish, Draupadī. Therefore anger leads to the destruction and non-existence of creatures.

sanskrit: yasmāt tu loke dṛśyante kṣamiṇaḥ pṛthivīsamāḥ tasmāj janma ca bhūtānāṃ bhavaś ca pratipadyate
english: But because patient men, steadfast as the earth, are seen in the world, therefore the birth and existence of creatures continues.

sanskrit: kṣantavyaṃ puruṣeṇeha sarvāsv āpatsu śobhane kṣamā bhavo hi bhūtānāṃ janma caiva prakīrtitam
english: A man must be forbearing in all adversities in this world, O beautiful one. For forbearance is proclaimed to be the very existence and birth of all beings.

sanskrit: ākruṣṭas tāḍitaḥ kruddhaḥ kṣamate yo balīyasā yaś ca nityaṃ jitakrodho vidvān uttamapūruṣaḥ
english: He who, though reviled and struck and enraged, forbears against one stronger than himself, and who is always one who has conquered anger — that learned man is the highest of persons.

sanskrit: prabhāvavān api naras tasya lokāḥ sanātanāḥ krodhanas tv alpavijñānaḥ pretya ceha ca naśyati
english: Even if a man is powerful, eternal worlds are his reward. But the wrathful man of little wisdom perishes both after death and here in this world.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmā gāthā nityaṃ kṣamāvatām gītāḥ kṣamāvatā kṛṣṇe kāśyapena mahātmanā
english: On this very point they cite these verses, eternally belonging to the forbearing — sung by the great-souled Kāśyapa who himself possessed forbearance, O Kṛṣṇā.

sanskrit: kṣamā dharmaḥ kṣamā yajñaḥ kṣamā vedāḥ kṣamā śrutam yas tām evaṃ vijānāti sa sarvaṃ kṣantum arhati
english: Forbearance is dharma; forbearance is sacrifice; forbearance is the Vedas; forbearance is sacred learning. He who knows it thus is worthy of bearing all things.

sanskrit: kṣamā brahma kṣamā satyaṃ kṣamā bhūtaṃ ca bhāvi ca kṣamā tapaḥ kṣamā śaucaṃ kṣamayā coddhṛtaṃ jagat
english: Forbearance is Brahman; forbearance is truth; forbearance is what has been and what will be; forbearance is austerity; forbearance is purity; and by forbearance the world is upheld.

sanskrit: ati brahmavidāṃ lokān ati cāpi tapasvinām ati yajñavidāṃ caiva kṣamiṇaḥ prāpnuvanti tān
english: The forbearing surpass the worlds of those who know Brahman, and the worlds of the ascetics, and even those of the knowers of sacrifice.

sanskrit: kṣamā tejasvināṃ tejaḥ kṣamā brahma tapasvinām kṣamā satyaṃ satyavatāṃ kṣamā dānaṃ kṣamā yaśaḥ
english: Forbearance is the energy of the energetic; forbearance is Brahman for the ascetics; forbearance is truth for the truthful; forbearance is charity; forbearance is renown.

sanskrit: tāṃ kṣamām īdṛśīṃ kṛṣṇe katham asmadvidhas tyajet yasyāṃ brahma ca satyaṃ ca yajñā lokāś ca viṣṭhitāḥ bhujyante yajvanāṃ lokāḥ kṣamiṇām apare tathā
english: How could one like me abandon such forbearance, O Kṛṣṇā — forbearance in which Brahman, truth, sacrifices, and all the worlds are established? The worlds of sacrificers are enjoyed by sacrificers, and those other worlds likewise by the forbearing.

sanskrit: kṣantavyam eva satataṃ puruṣeṇa vijānatā yadā hi kṣamate sarvaṃ brahma saṃpadyate tadā
english: A wise man must always be forbearing. For when one forbears all things, he attains to Brahman.

sanskrit: kṣamāvatām ayaṃ lokaḥ paraś caiva kṣamāvatām iha saṃmānam ṛcchanti paratra ca śubhāṃ gatim
english: This world belongs to the forbearing, and the next world too belongs to the forbearing. Here they attain honor, and in the beyond they attain an auspicious course.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ manyur manuṣyāṇāṃ kṣamayā nihataḥ sadā teṣāṃ paratare lokās tasmāt kṣāntiḥ parā matā
english: Those men whose anger is always slain by forbearance — they attain the highest worlds. Therefore forbearance is considered supreme.

sanskrit: iti gītāḥ kāśyapena gāthā nityaṃ kṣamāvatām śrutvā gāthāḥ kṣamāyās tvaṃ tuṣya draupadi mā krudhaḥ
english: Thus were sung by Kāśyapa these verses, eternally belonging to the forbearing. Having heard these verses on forbearance, be content, Draupadī — do not be angry.

sanskrit: pitāmahaḥ śāṃtanavaḥ śamaṃ saṃpūjayiṣyati ācāryo viduraḥ kṣattā śamam eva vadiṣyataḥ kṛpaś ca saṃjayaś caiva śamam eva vadiṣyataḥ
english: The grandfather, the son of Śaṃtanu, will honor peace; the preceptor, Vidura the Kṣattā, will counsel peace; and Kṛpa and Saṃjaya will likewise counsel peace.

sanskrit: somadatto yuyutsuś ca droṇaputras tathaiva ca pitāmahaś ca no vyāsaḥ śamaṃ vadati nityaśaḥ
english: Somadatta, Yuyutsu, and the son of Droṇa likewise, and our grandfather Vyāsa — all speak of peace always.

sanskrit: etair hi rājā niyataṃ codyamānaḥ śamaṃ prati rājyaṃ dāteti me buddhir na cel lobhān naśiṣyati
english: Being constantly urged toward peace by these men, it is my belief that the king will return the kingdom — unless greed destroys him.

sanskrit: kālo 'yaṃ dāruṇaḥ prāpto bharatānām abhūtaye niścitaṃ me sadaivaitat purastād api bhāmini
english: This dreadful time has come for the destruction of the Bhāratas — this I have always known with certainty, even from before, O passionate one.

sanskrit: suyodhano nārhatīti kṣamām evaṃ na vindati arhas tasyāham ity eva tasmān māṃ vindate kṣamā
english: Suyodhana does not find forbearance thus, thinking "he does not deserve it." But I think "I am worthy of it" — and therefore forbearance finds me.

sanskrit: etad ātmavatāṃ vṛttam eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ kṣamā caivānṛśaṃsyaṃ ca tat kartāsmy aham añjasā
english: This is the conduct of the self-possessed; this is the eternal dharma — forbearance and non-cruelty. I will practice this straightforwardly.

sanskrit: draupady uvāca namo dhātre vidhātre ca yau mohaṃ cakratus tava pitṛpaitāmahe vṛtte voḍhavye te 'nyathā matiḥ
english: Draupadī said: Homage to Dhātar and Vidhātar, who have created delusion in you! For when your ancestral and patrimonial duty should have been upheld, your mind has turned otherwise.

sanskrit: neha dharmānṛśaṃsyābhyāṃ na kṣāntyā nārjavena ca puruṣaḥ śriyam āpnoti na ghṛṇitvena karhi cit
english: A man does not attain prosperity here by dharma and non-cruelty, nor by forbearance, nor by straightforwardness, nor ever by compassion.

sanskrit: tvāṃ ced vyasanam abhyāgād idaṃ bhārata duḥsaham yat tvaṃ nārhasi nāpīme bhrātaras te mahaujasaḥ
english: If this unbearable misfortune has come upon you, O Bhārata — misfortune that neither you nor these your mighty brothers deserve —

sanskrit: na hi te 'dhyagamaj jātu tadānīṃ nādya bhārata dharmāt priyataraṃ kiṃ cid api cej jīvitād iha
english: — for neither then nor now, O Bhārata, has there ever been anything dearer to you than dharma — even dearer than life itself —

sanskrit: dharmārtham eva te rājyaṃ dharmārthaṃ jīvitaṃ ca te brāhmaṇā guravaś caiva jānanty api ca devatāḥ
english: — your kingdom is for the sake of dharma, and your very life is for the sake of dharma — the Brāhmaṇas, the elders, and the gods all know this —

sanskrit: bhīmasenārjunau caiva mādreyau ca mayā saha tyajes tvam iti me buddhir na tu dharmaṃ parityajeḥ
english: — it is my belief that you would abandon Bhīmasena, Arjuna, the sons of Mādrī, and even me, but that you would not abandon dharma.

sanskrit: rājānaṃ dharmagoptāraṃ dharmo rakṣati rakṣitaḥ iti me śrutam āryāṇāṃ tvāṃ tu manye na rakṣati
english: "Dharma, when protected, protects the king who guards dharma" — thus have I heard from the noble ones. But I believe dharma does not protect you.

sanskrit: ananyā hi naravyāghra nityadā dharmam eva te buddhiḥ satatam anveti chāyeva puruṣaṃ nijā
english: For your mind, O tiger among men, is single-mindedly fixed on dharma forever; it follows you always like a man's own shadow.

sanskrit: nāvamaṃsthā hi sadṛśān nāvarāñ śreyasaḥ kutaḥ avāpya pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ na te śṛṅgam avardhata
english: You never despised your equals, much less those who were better than you. Having obtained the entire earth, your pride never grew.

sanskrit: svāhākāraiḥ svadhābhiś ca pūjābhir api ca dvijān daivatāni pitṝṃś caiva satataṃ pārtha sevase
english: With svāhā-offerings, svadhā-offerings, and acts of worship, O Pārtha, you perpetually honored the twice-born, the deities, and the ancestors.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ sarvakāmais te satataṃ pārtha tarpitāḥ yatayo mokṣiṇaś caiva gṛhasthāś caiva bhārata
english: The Brāhmaṇas were always gratified by you with all their desires, O Pārtha; the ascetics, those intent on liberation, and the householders too, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: āraṇyakebhyo lauhāni bhājanāni prayacchasi nādeyaṃ brāhmaṇebhyas te gṛhe kiṃ cana vidyate
english: You give iron vessels to the forest-dwellers; there is nothing in your house that cannot be given to Brāhmaṇas.
